task: Fuse the accepted integer Selector scorer and packed v4 token selector into one on-chip HLS top

contract.score_q: local on-chip uint16 buffer[G]; NOT a top-level port and never DDR
contract.outputs: accepted selector 5 segments: out_tokens + group_index + source_type + region_id + valid, plus scale_out/output_count/real_count/context_count
contract.reuse: the two accepted translation units are #include'd into the wrapper; is_scorer_core<> (anonymous namespace) is called directly and token_selector_core_packed is called directly; no second copy of the maths

wv.note: reused by SHA, never retrained; scale is a positive common factor and is omitted

real_grounding_correct.tokens_source: xorshift64* (accepted NPZ has no raw tokens)

transfer_audit_correction.review_finding: The FPGA -> Jetson total applied one trailing 64 B align_up to selected_tokens + metadata instead of the frozen 5-segment per-offset alignment, so K=48/K=96 output bytes and the network/DDR times derived from them were underestimated.
transfer_audit_correction.fix: tools/transfer_audit.py::image_bytes now calls the frozen evaluation.hardware_regular_token_selector.fpga_transfer_layout(budget)/describe_fpga_layout(budget) live; fixed_budget_arena_bytes is authoritative and every reported network/DDR FPGA -> Jetson time is based on it.
deprecated_fields: fpga_to_jetson.total (old single-align value; no longer produced)
transfer_audit_correction.identity_bypass_note: G=80/K=96 reports output_count=80 (logical payload) and the fixed arena of the runtime budget K=96 separately.

limitations: csynth_design only: not C/RTL cosimulation, not place-and-route, not a bitstream, not a board measurement; timing/latency/resource numbers are synthesis estimates and the per-configuration cycle counts are formula-derived.
The on-chip fusion removes the intermediate score_q FPGA-DDR round trip; it does not remove the Jetson <-> FPGA round trip of the inputs/outputs.
The transfer audit is a model with an explicit bandwidth assumption and a sensitivity band; it is not a measured link throughput.
group_mean_q is still a separate input; reconstructing it from tokens_q in the PL is only quantified as a future saving and the accepted group-mean quantisation contract is unchanged this round.
The derived model is conservative (1.6% above the tool's worst case at the maximum compile-time bounds) but is still an estimate, not a measurement.

Codex review correction (2026-10-03): the first transfer audit used a single trailing align_up for FPGA -> Jetson and underestimated K=48/K=96. The deprecated transfer totals/times are void; only fixed_budget_arena_bytes / logical_payload_bytes and the arena-based times are authoritative. The HLS functional/timing/resource evidence is untouched and the decision is unchanged.
